Run cancer-registry quality tests

Source: R/cr_test.R
cr_test.Rd

cr_test() provides one entry point for the registry-level statistical tests implemented by compare_mi(), compare_mv(), and compare_rate(). For quality data, the default runs the M:I and MV% tests. For an asr object, the default runs incidence and mortality rate tests.

Usage

cr_test(
  x,
  test = c("all", "mi", "mv", "inci", "mort"),
  reference = NULL,
  standard = "wld85",
  alpha = 0.05,
  multiplier = 1e+05,
  variance_scale = c("display", "unmultiplied")
)

Arguments

x

An object with class quality or qualities, typically returned by create_quality(), or an object with class asr/asrs returned by create_asr().

test

The test to run. "all" runs M:I and MV% for quality data, or incidence and mortality rate tests for ASR data. "mi" and "mv" select quality tests; "inci" and "mort" select CI5-style rate tests.

reference

An optional external reference table passed to the selected comparison. For mi and mv, it must contain the required counts; for inci and mort, it must contain the selected rate and variance columns. CI5-XII incidence data alone do not contain death counts or MV counts and cannot be used directly for the first two tests.

standard

Standard-population suffix used by the rate test. Defaults to "wld85". Use "cr" for crude rates.

alpha

A single numeric significance level strictly between 0 and 1. Defaults to 0.05.

multiplier

Rate multiplier used only for legacy unmultiplied rate variances. Defaults to 100000.

variance_scale

Scale of rate variance columns passed to compare_rate(). The default, "display", matches current create_asr() output; use "unmultiplied" for legacy variance columns.

Value

A tibble containing the selected result for a single test. With test = "all", a named list with class cr_tests is returned.

Examples

quality_data <- structure(
  data.frame(
    regicode = c("A", "B", "C", "D"),
    year = "2024",
    sex = "1",
    cancer = "101",
    fbs = c(100, 100, 150, 200),
    sws = c(80, 40, 75, 80),
    mv = c(95, 70, 80, 75)
  ),
  class = c("quality", "data.frame")
)
tests <- cr_test(quality_data)
tests$mi
#> # A tibble: 4 × 15
#>   regicode year  sex   cancer   fbs   sws    mi reference_n theta   phi     z2
#>   <chr>    <chr> <chr> <chr>  <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>       <int> <dbl> <dbl>  <dbl>
#> 1 A        2024  1     101      100    80   0.8           3 0.433 0.788 21.9  
#> 2 B        2024  1     101      100    40   0.4           3 0.522 6.19   0.330
#> 3 C        2024  1     101      150    75   0.5           3 0.5   7.14   0    
#> 4 D        2024  1     101      200    80   0.4           3 0.557 4.82   1.31 
#> # ℹ 4 more variables: p_value <dbl>, critical_value <dbl>, unusual <lgl>,
#> #   status <chr>
